resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 confirmed. The live aramco.com press release timed out repeatedly on url_verifier; its Wayback capture verifies (200 + '2028'). Aramco's 2024 $25bn MGS-expansion release states the additional 3.15 bscfd capacity comes online 'by 2028'. BlackRidge Research project profile independently gives 'Project Completion Date: Q4 2028' for MGS-3 (which includes the EWJZG-1 STS-1->Shoqaiq segment). Two independent sources agree on 2028.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia confirmed. Both sources explicitly name the segment: BlackRidge quotes 'Lay 56-inch diameter pipeline (EWJZG-1) from Sector Two STS-1 to Shoqaiq (462 km)' within MGS-3, 'one of the largest oil and gas pipeline projects in Saudi Arabia owned by Saudi Aramco'. DMS Projects lists 'Sector II STS 1 to Shuqaiq Pipeline (EWJZG-1)' under Saudi Arabia. Shoqaiq/Shuqaiq (Ash Shuqayq, Red Sea coast) and the STS-1 origin are both inside Saudi Arabia; two independent aggregators agree.

Owner1=Aramco 100% confirmed. The Aramco 2024 release describes the Master Gas System expansion as Aramco's own program (contract awards it is making); Wayback capture verifies (200 + 'Aramco'/'2028'). BlackRidge and DMS Projects both state the MGS-3 project (incl. EWJZG-1 STS-1->Shoqaiq) is owned/operated by Saudi Aramco. As Aramco's flagship national gas grid, 100% Aramco ownership is consistent across sources; no conflicting owner found.
